title.narrative: Emergency response to cholera outbreak in Renk (Cordaid funds)

description.narrative: Beneficiaries Women Men Children Elderly Persons with disability Direct Beneficiaries 48,382 50,357 103,801 10,127 40,507

Cordaid would like to consider provision of effective cholera treatment and prevention services to vulnerable populations through set up oral rehydration points (ORPs), cholera treatment facilities (CTUs/CTCs), and health care workers training on treatment protocols. Adequate supplies are available and job aids are in place. Cordaid will ensure that ORPs and CTUs/CTCs are accessible to the most-affected populations, work closely with epidemiology and logistics to predict supply needs and pre-position them as needed. And to ensure effective case management Cordaid will train health-care workers on the use of RDTs, specimen collection and transport procedures. The project team will work closely with WASH and logistics colleagues to ensure adequate IPC in treatment structures

South Sudan is one of the cholera endemic countries in the Africa region, the country has so far experienced ten (10) major cholera outbreaks (1980 – 2017) of varying magnitude from 17 to 48,035 cases, with case fatality rates (CFR) ranging between 0.13% and 2.9%.. The key drivers to cholera outbreaks include poor WASH conditions, complex humanitarian conditions and changing climatic patterns worsening socio-economic conditions. South Sudanese continue to face challenges of access to safe and clean water and 59% of the population have no access to safe and clean drinking water. In addition, 60% of the population practice open defecation. On 8th October the government of Republic of South Sudan received report of suspected cholera case and on 28th October the government of South Sudan declared cholera outbreak in Renk County of Upper Nile State. . As of 30th December 2024 a cumulative total number of 9,707have been reported with 180 death CRF of 1.9%. Cordaid is running two Cholera treatment Units . This project aims to reduce the incidence and spread of cholera in Mayom, Guit and Pariang Counties, South Sudan, by targeting 37,976 vulnerable individuals, including refugees, returnees, and host communities in high-risk areas. To reduce the incidence and spread of cholera, we will employ a multi-sectoral approach focusing on rapid response and Containment of the outbreak by enhancing surveilance using the trained health workers, provision of infection prevention and control (IPC) supplies and maintaining the IPC measures, setting up of Oral rehydration therapy (ORT) points, carry out contact tracing and conduct Oral Cholera Vaccination (ORV) campaigns when vaccines are readily available. The Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) intervention will focus on Provision of household water treatment purifiers, construction of semi-permanent units of latrines at cholera treatment units and and we will scale risk communication and community engagement (RC&CE) to raise awareness on cholera outbreak and improve hygiene practices by providing supplies such as multi-Purpose laundry soap, Buckets for water collection and storage and handwashing stations. The project will be implemented jointly by Cordaid and Africa Development Aid (ADA) over a six-month period, starting in 1st February 2025, subject to timely resource availability. A robust M&E system will be in place to ensure quality assurance and accountability. We will monitor key indicators, conduct regular field visits, and analyze data to inform decision-making and adapt our strategies as needed. To ensure long-term sustainability, we will focus on capacity building of local communities, including health workers and hygiene promoters. We will also promote community ownership of interventions, such as through community-led maintenance of sanitation facilities. Additionally, we will strengthen partnerships with local authorities and other organizations to ensure continued support and resource allocation for health services in Mayom, Guit and Pariang Counties.
